drivers.name: Barco ClickShare CX
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Wireless presentation Base Unit control via local REST API V2 (HTTPS, port 4003). Live sharing/standby state over the API's event streams, standby / wake / reboot, audio + video + wallpaper + CEC, paired-button readback. Covers CX-20 / CX-30 / CX-50, C-5 / C-10 / C-10A, CB-Core / CB-Pro.

help.overview: The ClickShare Base Unit exposes a local REST API on port 4003 (HTTPS). Use this driver to mirror runtime status (is anyone sharing?), force the Base Unit into / out of standby, reboot, and switch audio output / wallpaper / video mode under macro control. Typical room logic: when the room shutdown macro fires, send `standby`; when the room comes up, send `wakeup` (or rely on the Base Unit's auto-wake on first share).
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP (or DHCP reservation) on the Base Unit — its
   Ethernet MAC is on the bottom label. Leave port 4003 open between
   the OpenAVC server and the Base Unit.
2. In the Base Unit's web Configurator (https://<base-unit>), open
   Security → Pin Code / API and confirm the API is enabled. Default
   credentials are integrator / integrator. Change them and supply
   the new ones below.
3. (Recommended) Replace the self-signed HTTPS certificate with one
   trusted by the OpenAVC host, then flip "Verify SSL Certificate"
   on. The driver works either way; verifying is just defense in
   depth.
4. Click Save. State changes stream in live over the API's event
   subscriptions — someone starting to share shows up immediately.
   The 30-second poll is a background resync; there is no need to
   shorten it.

compatible_models.notes: Same V2 REST API across the entire CX / C / CB family. Feature differences (number of paired buttons, dual video outputs on CX-50 Gen2, UVC pass-through on CX-30 Gen2 / CX-50 Gen2) are reported by the Base Unit at runtime in the `supportedOutputs`, `supportedModes`, `supportedPowerModes`, etc. arrays — the driver doesn't need to know the model. Older CSE / CSC ClickShare units use a different (legacy) API and are NOT covered.

drivers.name: Blackmagic Streaming Encoder
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Blackmagic Streaming Encoder HD and 4K (formerly Web Presenter HD and 4K) over the Blackmagic Streaming Encoder Ethernet Protocol (TCP 9977): start and stop the live stream, choose the platform, server, quality and video mode, set the stream key, and see the stream's status, bitrate and duration as the encoder reports them.

help.overview: Blackmagic Streaming Encoder HD and 4K (formerly Web Presenter HD and 4K) over TCP 9977. Start and stop the live stream; choose the streaming platform, server, quality and video mode from the lists the encoder offers; set the stream key, passphrase or URL; choose the monitor output's audio and which connection streams when a phone is tethered. The encoder reports every change as it happens; the bitrate, duration and cache use are read every poll.
help.setup:
1. Give the encoder a fixed IP address (in Blackmagic Streaming Setup, on the Setup tab) and enter it here. Control uses TCP 9977, which needs no login.
2. Platforms loaded from a streaming XML file appear in the platform list beside the built-in ones; load them with Blackmagic Streaming Setup.
3. The stream key is never shown here: the device page says only whether one is set.

compatible_models.notes: Built from the Blackmagic Streaming Encoder Ethernet Protocol v1.2 (January 2026). The 4K streams Ultra HD; the HD streams up to 1080p. The encoder lists its own video modes, platforms, servers and quality levels.
The same units under their name before 2025; the Web Presenter manual (May 2024) documents the same v1.2 protocol. Not the original Web Presenter, which has no streaming.

drivers.name: BrightSign Player (Local DWS)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Monitors and controls BrightSign signage players through the player's Local Diagnostic Web Server API: identity, health, clock, every HDMI output with its display and video mode, HDMI power-save, reboot, snapshot, CEC, registry and log level, plus the Moka display's own panel controls. Drives the presentation with UDP messages and sets its User Variables.

help.overview: BrightSign players run a presentation from BrightSign Author (or a web page) and are managed through BrightSign Cloud. This driver talks to one player on the local network through its Local Diagnostic Web Server API: it reports the player's identity, health, clock and video mode, lists every HDMI output with the connected display's state, and can put an output to sleep, reboot the player, take a snapshot of what is playing, send a CEC payload, read and write the registry and change the log level. The presentation itself is driven the way BrightSign Author expects: a UDP message to the port the presentation listens on, which a UDP Input event in the presentation matches, and <variable>:<value> messages that set its User Variables. On a Moka display with a built-in player the display's power, volume, brightness, contrast, standby timeout, video output and white balance are settings too.
help.setup:
1. Turn on the player's Local Diagnostic Web Server. In BrightSign Author, create or edit a Setup file (Admin > Setup), tick Enable Local Diagnostic Web Server under Player Settings > Player Configuration, enter a password, and provision the player with it. Players on BrightSignOS 9.0.218 / 9.1.75 or later have it off by default; older ones have it on with the serial number as the password. A cloud-managed player can also be switched under Network > Properties.
2. Enter the player's IP address. Leave Use HTTPS on and the port at 443 for BrightSignOS 9.0.218 / 9.1.52 or later; an older player that still serves plain HTTP uses port 80 with Use HTTPS off.
3. The username is always admin. Enter the password from the setup file, or the player's serial number if none was set. Leave it blank only for a player set up with no authentication.
4. To control the presentation, set the UDP Port to the UDP Receiver Port in the presentation's settings (Presentation Settings > Interactive > Networking in BrightSign Author) and add UDP Input events for the messages you will send.
5. Local DWS access is over the local network only; a player reached through BrightSign Cloud is out of reach of this driver.
help.connection: Enable the Local Diagnostic Web Server in the player's setup file first; user admin, password from the setup file or the serial number.

compatible_models.notes: Every Series 3 to Series 6 player on BrightSignOS 8.4.6 or later with the Local Diagnostic Web Server enabled. The XC2055 and XT2145 expose two HDMI outputs and the XC4055 four; the driver reads the count from the player.
A display with a built-in player. The Display settings and the Display Power actions use the display-control API, which needs BrightSignOS 9.0.189 or later.

drivers.name: Crestron AirMedia Series 3
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Crestron AirMedia Series 3 wireless presentation receivers over the receiver's API: who is connected and presenting, the login code, the source on the display, the HDMI output, the USB conferencing peripherals and their volume, the paired AirMedia Connect adaptors, and the presentation settings. Changes arrive as the receiver reports them.

help.overview: Controls a Crestron AirMedia Series 3 receiver: see who is connected and presenting, show the login code on a panel, disconnect everyone at the end of a meeting, turn the HDMI output off and on, set and mute the USB speaker used for wireless conferencing, and follow the paired AirMedia Connect adaptors. The receiver chooses what is on the display by its Routing Mode.
help.setup:
1. Sign in to the receiver's web page once (https:// and its IP address, shown on the display). A new receiver asks for a new administrator username and password there.
2. Enter that username and password here.
3. Leave Verify TLS Certificate off unless a trusted certificate is installed on the receiver.
help.connection: Check the receiver's IP address on its welcome screen, and that the username and password are an administrator account on the receiver.

compatible_models.notes: Built from the API for AirMedia Series 3 Receivers (firmware 3.0800.0157) and tested against the simulator. The commands and readings a model lacks are left off: no wireless conferencing on the AM-3000-WF, no HDMI input on the AM-3000-WF and AM-3100-WF, no AirMedia Connect adaptors on the AM-3200 and AM-3200-GV.

drivers.name: Epiphan Pearl
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Epiphan Pearl Nano, Mini, Nexus and Pearl-2 lecture-capture and live production systems over the Pearl REST API: start and stop recording and streaming for the whole unit, a channel or one stream, switch layouts, add bookmarks, set input gain, mute and phantom power, pick the HDMI output source, run CMS events (Kaltura, Panopto, Opencast), apply configuration presets, and watch storage, uploads, CPU and temperature.

help.overview:
Epiphan Pearl is a hardware encoder that records and streams several channels at once, each composed from the unit's inputs by a layout.

OpenAVC starts and stops recording (every recorder, or one), starts and stops streams (every stream, one channel's, or one stream), switches a channel's layout, drops bookmarks into a recording, sets input gain, mute, phantom power and delays, picks what the HDMI output shows, controls scheduled CMS events, applies configuration presets and reboots the unit. Live state covers every recorder and stream, the one-touch control, storage, file uploads, CPU load and temperature.

Each channel is also a Video Panel source over RTSP once its port is entered under Channel RTSP Ports.
help.setup:
1. Enter the Pearl's IP address. The REST API answers on the web port: 80, or 443 with Use HTTPS when HTTPS is enabled on the Pearl.
2. Enter the admin account's password (Pearl firmware 4.14.2 and later require one on every account).
3. For channel previews in the Video Panel, open the channel's Status page in the Pearl Admin panel, read the RTSP stream URL's port and enter it under Channel RTSP Ports. The Pearl Nano's channel is always 554.
4. Stream destinations, layouts and CMS settings are created in the Pearl Admin panel; this driver starts, stops and switches them.
help.connection: Check the admin password and whether HTTPS is enabled on the Pearl (then tick Use HTTPS and set the port to 443).

compatible_models.notes: Built from the Pearl device REST API v2.0. The Pearl Nano has one channel and one layout; multi-channel commands act on that one.

drivers.name: Magewell Ultra Encode
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Ultra Encode streaming and recording, individual destinations, audio paths, video encoding, overlays and schedules.

help.overview: Controls configured streaming and recording sessions, reports their actual progress and errors, and exposes audio and video controls. Configure destination addresses, storage and schedules in the encoder’s web interface; they appear here after Refresh Status.
help.setup: Use firmware V2.5.62 and enter an encoder account with control permission. Username is case-sensitive. HTTP uses port 80; if HTTPS is enabled, select HTTPS and its configured port. Configure stream destinations and recording channels in the web interface. Start Streaming/Recording controls the global function; each desired destination/channel must also be enabled. An optional RTSP or SRT preview URL can be copied from the encoder’s Live page. No hardware qualification has been performed.

compatible_models.notes: HTTP API with JSON POST login on firmware V2.5.62. Input switching and composition are AIO-only.
Current Rev B hardware only: SKUs 531100000 and 531200000, firmware V2.5.62. Discontinued Rev A models are not supported.

drivers.name: Mersive Solstice Pod
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Mersive Solstice Pods (and Solstice Windows Software) over the OpenControl REST API. Boot users, clear posts, suspend and wake the display, reset the on-screen key, push bulletin or emergency banners, and monitor connected users and post counts.

help.overview:
Mersive Solstice is a wireless presentation system. Users share screens, video, and media from laptops, phones, and tablets to a Solstice Pod that drives the room display.

OpenAVC controls the Pod's runtime: clear posts, boot all users at end-of-meeting, sleep / wake the display, reset the on-screen connection key, and push bulletin or emergency banners. Live state includes connected users, active posts, bandwidth, and the current screen key.

Install-time configuration (network setup, calendar integration, splash-screen images) stays in the Solstice Dashboard. RS-232 pass-thru is exposed for chained-display control via a USB-to-serial adapter on the Pod.
help.setup:
1. Confirm the Pod has Solstice Enterprise Edition. The OpenControl API is gated to Enterprise hosts.
2. In the Solstice Dashboard, set an admin password (strongly recommended — without one, any device on the network can drive this Pod).
3. Enter the Pod's IP address and admin password here. Default port is 80 (HTTP). Tick Use HTTPS for port 443; Solstice ships with a self-signed certificate which the driver does not verify.
4. Mersive recommends polling no more than once every 10 seconds. The default interval is 30 s; the minimum is 10 s.

compatible_models.notes: Requires Solstice Enterprise Edition license — Standard Edition Pods do not expose the OpenControl API. Some commands are Pod-only (reboot, hardware variant, HDMI input force-off); Windows Software hosts ignore them. Power-management / suspend / wake are Pod-only.

drivers.name: Roku (ECP)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Roku streaming players and Roku TVs over the local network using the External Control Protocol (ECP). Full remote surface, text entry, app launch/install, and TV power, volume, input, and tuner control on supported models.

help.overview: Controls Roku streaming players and Roku TVs over the local network using Roku's External Control Protocol (ECP). Provides the full remote-control surface (navigation, transport, search, and on-screen text entry), app launch and install, and TV power, volume, input, and tuner control on supported models. Reports power state, the currently active app, and media playback status. No Roku account, PIN, or cloud connection is required, and it works with third-party Roku TVs too.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Roku to the same network and note its IP address (Settings > Network > About, or the Roku mobile app).
2. On the Roku, set Settings > System > Control by mobile apps > Network access to 'Default' or 'Permissive' (NOT 'Disabled'). Roku OS 14.1 and later block remote key presses when this is off; the driver then reports Mobile Control Enabled = false and key presses return HTTP 403.
3. Enter the IP address. The port is 8060 (do not change).
4. No PIN, password, or account is needed.
5. To launch an app, use Launch App with its channel ID. Find an installed app's ID by opening it and reading the Active App ID state, or browse http://<roku-ip>:8060/query/apps in a browser. Common IDs: Netflix 12, Amazon Prime Video 13.

compatible_models.notes: Any Roku device with 'Control by mobile apps' enabled, including third-party Roku TVs (TCL, Hisense, onn, etc.). Power, volume, and input/tuner keys apply to models that report supports-tv-power-control.

drivers.name: WolfVision Cynap
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls WolfVision Cynap presentation and collaboration systems (Cynap Pro, Cynap Core Pro, Cynap Pure Mini on firmware 1.7x) over WolfProt: standby and Wake-on-LAN, volume and mutes, freeze, the four presentation windows, opening an HDMI input or the whiteboard, recording and streaming, ending a presentation, and status pushed as it changes.

help.overview: WolfVision Cynap presentation systems over WolfProt (TCP 50915). Standby and Wake-on-LAN, master volume and mute, microphone mute, freeze, the four presentation windows, HDMI inputs and the whiteboard, recording and streaming, and status the Cynap reports as it changes. Polls every 15 seconds as well.
help.setup:
1. Give the Cynap a fixed IP address and enter it. Control uses TCP 50915; for TLS, turn on TLS and use port 50917.
2. Login: with no moderator password on the Cynap, leave the password blank. If the Cynap requires a moderator password (Settings > Login), enter it with Access Level User. Changing the device name, presentation mode, power-down mode, output 2 mode or restarting needs Access Level Admin and the administrator password (and the Admin Remote PIN if the Cynap asks for one).
3. Power On from standby uses Wake-on-LAN: the MAC address is read from the Cynap when it first connects. Standby closes the Cynap's connections, so it shows offline until it is woken. A Power Down Mode of Shutdown may not wake on the network.

compatible_models.notes: Firmware 1.7x (built from the 1.78a WolfProt reference). Two HDMI outputs, recording and streaming.
Firmware 1.7x. Commands for features this model lacks (recording, a second output) are refused by the unit.
